summary: Task 3 delivers exactly the persistence shape specified in the tech-spec Data Models section: Bot @Document with three @CompoundIndex declarations matching the spec byte-for-byte, BotStatus enum with the correct Jackson-only lowercase wire form (leaving Mongo persistence as name() so the partial filter expression keeps matching), and BotRepository with the three required derived queries. Patterns mirror Project.java (bean-style mutables, @Indexed on the FK, same @CompoundIndexes wrapper) and tests rigorously cover both repository semantics and partial-unique-index enforcement plus presence. No business logic leaked into this layer — the task scope is respected.

suggestions.suggestion: BotRepositoryTest uses the fully qualified `org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat(...)` inside `.assertNext(...)` callbacks instead of the already-static-imported short form available everywhere else. BotIndexTest at lines 17/93/96/99/100/103/104/107/116/122 demonstrates the project convention — `import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;` and call `assertThat(...)` bare. The FQN form is noisier and visually breaks the reactive assertion blocks.
suggestions.benefit: Consistent assertion style across the two new test files; lower noise inside StepVerifier callbacks.

suggestions.suggestion: `BotStatusJsonTest` constructs a vanilla `new ObjectMapper()` rather than reusing the Spring-configured Jackson bean. For this test that is intentional and correct — the goal is to assert the enum's @JsonValue/@JsonCreator contract independently of any global Jackson configuration — but a one-line comment explicitly stating the rationale ("verifying enum-level contract; not asserting Spring's ObjectMapper config") would prevent a future reviewer from 'fixing' it by autowiring the configured ObjectMapper, which would change what the test guarantees.
suggestions.benefit: Protects the intent of the test against well-meaning future edits.

suggestions.suggestion: `BotStatus.fromString` will throw `IllegalArgumentException` from `valueOf` when Jackson is asked to deserialise a malformed status value (e.g. `"pending"`, `null`, empty string, or wrong case after toUpperCase still not a member). That is acceptable today — Jackson wraps it into a `JsonMappingException` and `GlobalErrorHandler` translates it into a 400 — but for a clearer error surface and defensive null handling you could replace `valueOf` with an explicit switch over the two enumerated lowercase strings and throw a more descriptive `IllegalArgumentException`. Not blocking — the current behavior matches the spec literally and the only callers of this method are Jackson deserialisers controlled by validated DTOs.
suggestions.benefit: Slightly clearer error message on malformed wire input; explicit null handling.
